q1.q: Is a DocuFirma signature legally valid?
q1.a: Yes. It is an advanced electronic signature under Article 26 of the eIDAS Regulation, admissible as evidence in legal proceedings across the EU. For the few acts that legally require a qualified signature or a notarial deed, it does not replace those requirements.

q2.a: It is proof, issued by a qualified trust service provider, that a document existed with specific content at an exact date and time. Under Article 41 of eIDAS, the accuracy of that date and the integrity of the data are presumed.

q3.q: Does the signer need an account or to install anything?
q3.a: No. They receive an email with a unique link, review the document in their browser and sign with a finger, a stylus or the mouse. It works on phones, tablets and computers.

q4.q: Which biometric data is captured and how is it protected?
q4.a: We capture the signature stroke (coordinates, pressure, tilt and timing) with the signer's explicit consent. It is encrypted with AES-256, used only as evidence of the signature and kept for the period stated in the privacy policy.

q5.q: What happens if I don't use all my monthly signatures?
q5.a: Signatures included in the plan renew every billing cycle and do not roll over. Pack signatures never expire and are only used once your monthly signatures run out.

q6.a: One signature is one signer completing an envelope, even if they sign several documents at once. An envelope with three signers uses three signatures. If someone declines or the envelope expires, the pending signatures go back to your balance.

q7.q: Can I verify a signed document?
q7.a: Yes. On the verification page you can enter the DF-XXXX-XXXX code printed on the document or upload the PDF: we compute its fingerprint in your browser and check it against the sealed original, without the file ever leaving your device.

q8.a: Yes. You can cancel your subscription from your dashboard at any time. You keep access to your history and your signed documents.

q9.q: Can I strengthen the signer's identification?
q9.a: Yes. When preparing the envelope you can require, per signer, a one-time code we text to their mobile: without it they cannot sign. It adds a second factor (possession of the phone) to the email evidence. SMS codes are paid separately with SMS packs; each code sent uses 1 SMS.

q10.q: Can someone sign in person, at my office?
q10.a: Yes. Mark the signer as "In-person signing": they receive no email and you get a "Sign now" button on the envelope so they can sign on your tablet, phone or computer. The evidence certificate states that the signature was in person and before whom. You can combine it with the SMS code.

howItWorksPage.title: How DocuFirma works
howItWorksPage.subtitle: A process designed to make signing as easy as opening an email, without giving up legal guarantees.

senderSteps.s1: Create your account and upload one or more PDFs, images or Word documents.
senderSteps.s2: Add the signers with first name, last name and email. Choose whether they sign in parallel or in order, whether anyone signs in person next to you and whether they must confirm an SMS code.
senderSteps.s3: Track every envelope in real time and receive the signed PDF, the evidence certificate and the timestamp.

signerSteps.s1: Opens the link in the email, or signs on your device if they are with you: no account, nothing to install.
signerSteps.s2: Reviews the full document in the browser, on a phone or a computer.
signerSteps.s3: Accepts the consent, confirms the SMS code if you require it and signs on screen. Gets a signed copy instantly.

behind.hash: We compute the SHA-256 fingerprint of every original document.
behind.biometric: We capture the biometric stroke and store it encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
behind.pdf: We generate the signed PDF with the signature, the verification code and an evidence certificate.
behind.tsa: We request an RFC 3161 qualified timestamp over the final document.

privacy.description: How Cloudin Hosting S.L. processes the personal data of DocuFirma users and signers.

s1.p:
When data subjects provide data through the CLOUDIN websites, the Data Controller for the data provided is Cloudin Hosting S.L. In addition, depending on the reasons for contacting CLOUDIN, the data provided will be communicated to the company. For example, if the data subject provides their CV to be added to the job pool, their data will be communicated to the company.

CLOUDIN is committed to protecting the personal data of everyone whose data it processes, respecting the applicable legal requirements on data protection and with the highest guarantees of confidentiality and data security.

s2.h: For what purpose does the CLOUDIN group process personal data
s2.p:
Through the CLOUDIN websites, data may be collected from people who wish to ask questions about our services, request quotes for them or purchase products. The purpose of processing such data is to answer the enquiry made by the data subject.

If the data subject subscribes to our newsletters, they will receive our communications at the email address used to register until they decide to object to receiving them in the future.

The CLOUDIN websites may also include a Jobs section for data subjects who wish to add their CV to the CLOUDIN job pool and take part in our open selection processes. To learn more about how applications are processed, please consult the privacy notice for selection procedures.

s3.p: We process your account data (first name, last name, email, company, optional tax ID), billing data and usage data to provide the service (art. 6.1.b GDPR), to comply with legal obligations (art. 6.1.c) and to improve the service (legitimate interest, art. 6.1.f).

s4.p: For documents sent by our users, CLOUDIN acts as data processor through DocuFirma. We process first name, last name, email, mobile number (only if the sender turns on SMS verification), IP address, device data, approximate location and the events of the signing process to generate the signature evidence.

s5.p: The signature stroke (coordinates, pressure, tilt and timing) may constitute biometric data (art. 9 GDPR). It is only captured with the signer's explicit consent, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, used solely as proof of the signature and kept for 5 years from signing, unless legal proceedings require it to be kept longer. After that period it is deleted automatically.

s6.h: Legal basis for processing the data
s6.p:
The processing of data provided by data subjects to resolve the questions they raise through the various forms and contact channels on the CLOUDIN websites is based on CLOUDIN's legitimate interest in answering those questions.

The processing of the data subject's email address for the newsletter subscription is based on the consent of the owner of the email address.

s7.p: The data will not be disclosed to third parties unless required by law. Providers that serve CLOUDIN as data processors, listed in the section “Data processors for the DocuFirma service”, only access the data to provide the service and on our instructions.

s8.h: Data processors for the DocuFirma service
s8.p: To provide the DocuFirma service we use providers located in, or with servers in, the EU, acting as data processors: Supabase (database and storage, Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting, Frankfurt), Stripe (payments), Resend (email), Mensatek (qualified timestamping and SMS delivery) and Sentry (error monitoring). Any international transfer is covered by standard contractual clauses.

s9.p:
The retention period depends on the purpose for which the data were collected. If the data are processed to answer an enquiry, they will be kept until it has been answered. For a newsletter subscription, the data will be kept until the data subject asks to unsubscribe.

In DocuFirma, account data are kept while the account is active. Completed envelopes and their evidence are kept for 5 years to defend against possible claims. Invoices are kept for the periods required by tax law.

In any case, regardless of the retention periods applicable in each case, once the purpose of the processing has ended CLOUDIN will apply its data blocking and deletion policies.

s10.p:
Data subjects may exercise their rights at the addresses shown at the beginning of this policy or at the following email address of CLOUDIN's legal department: [hola@cloudin.pro](mailto:hola@cloudin.pro)

You can also contact our Data Protection Officer at the following email address: [hola@cloudin.pro](mailto:hola@cloudin.pro)

If data subjects consider that their rights have not been properly addressed, they may file a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency, in the case of Spain.

Specifically, in the case of Spain, data subjects may exercise their rights of access, rectification or erasure, portability, restriction and objection to the processing of their data.

In all countries, data subjects may withdraw their consent at any time, without retroactive effect, and may also object to receiving electronic communications from CLOUDIN through the link included in each communication.

cookies.description: What cookies are and which ones this website uses.

s1.p:
Cookies are small files that websites store in the browser of the user visiting them. They are necessary to bring countless advantages to web browsing in the provision of interactive services. These files allow amounts of data ranging from a few kilobytes to several megabytes to be stored on the user's device.

The following information about the possible types of cookies will help you better understand and assess our cookie policy:

- Session cookies: temporary cookies that remain on your device until you leave the website that uses them, so none is recorded on the user's disk. The information obtained through these cookies makes it possible to manage operations with each of the users accessing the website at the same time.
- Persistent cookies: cookies that remain stored in your device's cookie storage after you leave the website, and that the website will read again the next time you visit it, in order to remember information that makes browsing easier (for example, accessing the service directly without logging in) or to provide a commercial service (for example, offering products or services related to previous visits).

Cookies exchanged when browsing a website may be:

- First-party cookies: cookies generated by the website being visited.
- Third-party cookies: cookies received when browsing that website but generated by a third-party service hosted on it. One example is the cookie used by an advertisement or banner on the website we visit. Another is the cookie used by a visitor counter contracted by the website we visit.

Cookies may be used for different purposes:

- Technical purposes: they allow the user to browse a website, platform or application and use its various options or services, such as controlling traffic and data communication, identifying the session, accessing restricted areas, remembering the items in an order, completing the purchase of an order, applying to register for or take part in an event, using security features while browsing, storing content for broadcasting video or sound, or sharing content through social networks.
- Personalisation: they allow the user to access the service with certain predefined general features based on a series of criteria on the user's device, such as the language, the type of browser used to access the service, the regional settings from which it is accessed, etc.
- Analysis or performance: they allow whoever is responsible for them to track and analyse the behaviour of users of the websites to which they are linked. The information collected through this type of cookie is used to measure the activity of websites, applications or platforms and to build browsing profiles of their users, in order to make improvements based on the analysis of how users use the service.
- Behavioural advertising: they allow the most efficient possible management of the advertising spaces that the publisher may have included on a website, application or platform from which the requested service is provided. These cookies store information about user behaviour obtained through continuous observation of their browsing habits, which makes it possible to build a specific profile to show advertising based on it.

s2.h: We do not use non-exempt cookies
s2.p: You will not find a cookie banner. This website relies solely on functional cookies.

s3.p:
If you want to delete the cookies set by CloudIn from your browser, here are instructions for the different browsers:

- [Internet Explorer](https://support.microsoft.com/es-es/help/278835/how-to-delete-cookie-files-in-internet-explorer)
- [Microsoft Edge](https://support.microsoft.com/es-es/topic/eliminar-y-administrar-cookies-168dab11-0753-043d-7c16-ede5947fc64d)
- [Google Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95647?co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid&hl=es-419)
- [Firefox](https://support.mozilla.org/es/kb/Borrar%20cookies)
- [Safari](https://support.apple.com/es-es/HT201265)
- Others: in general, to delete cookies from your browser, go to the browser's Preferences or Settings menu and look for the Privacy section. There you will find options to manage your cookies and other data stored by the websites you visit, and to configure how your browser handles cookies.

s4.p: We also inform you that users may at any time reject or configure the use of cookies through the following types of settings, depending on how they browse.

signature-policy.description: How a signature is created, preserved and verified in DocuFirma.

s1.p: Biometric advanced electronic signature under Article 26 of Regulation (EU) 910/2014 (eIDAS), complemented by a qualified timestamp under its Articles 41 and 42.

s2.p: By default, the signer receives by email a unique link with 256 bits of entropy; only the SHA-256 hash of the link is stored. The sender may also require a 6-digit one-time code texted to the signer's mobile (valid for 10 minutes, with limited attempts; only its hash is stored), or that the signature takes place in person on the sender's own device, in which case no email link is sent and the certificate states before whom it was signed. Name, email, mobile number (if SMS is used), IP address, user agent, device, approximate location and the event timeline are recorded.

s3.p: After reviewing the whole document and accepting the consent (a versioned, recorded text), the signer draws their signature. For every point we capture coordinates, pressure, tilt, pointer type and a high-resolution timestamp.

s4.p: We compute the SHA-256 fingerprint of every original document, of the biometric file and of the final signed PDF. An RFC 3161 timestamp is requested from Mensatek (policy OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.5734.3.18.1) over the latter and over the evidence certificate.

s5.p: Anyone can verify a document at docufirma.es/verify with its code or fingerprint. The timestamp can be checked independently with OpenSSL (openssl ts -verify).

s6.p: Evidence is kept encrypted for 5 years. Access is restricted to server processes and, upon request, to judicial authorities.
